However, the subject land had not been acquired and, therefore, the petitioner has also not received any compensation for the same.
6. The petitioner essentially seeks that the possession of the land be returned to him, although no such prayer is being made in the present petition.
7. Issue notice.
8. Learned counsel for the respondent accepts notice and seeks time to take instructions and if necessary, file a counter-affidavit.
9. Let a counter-affidavit be filed within a period of four weeks from date.

Rejoinder thereto, if any,
be filed before the next date of hearing.
10. In the meanwhile, the petitioner is also at liberty to amend the writ petition, clearly reflecting the relief as sought by the petitioner.
11. The petitioner shall also take steps to implead the beneficiary, Delhi Development Authority (DDA) which is currently in possession of the subject land.

12. List on 24.10.2024.
